content.title: About
content.content: The chocolate cookie bar is a soft, chewy cookie coated with a layer of milk or dark chocolate. It combines a crisp wheat‑based base, a lightly sweet interior, and a rich chocolate aroma. Individually wrapped, it makes a convenient snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first chocolate bar was introduced in the United States in the early 20th century.
Chocolate in cookies often contains a small amount of cocoa butter, which improves melt‑in‑the‑mouth texture.
Cookie bars are frequently used as rewards in schools and offices.
There are many variations: with nuts, dried fruit, caramel, or plain.
In Russia, these bars are commonly sold in 30‑50 g packages.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Carbohydrates from flour and sugar provide quick energy, useful during short breaks.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Chocolate is rich in flavonoids that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Magnesium content
items.content: Magnesium present in cocoa supports muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Small amount of iron
items.content: A chocolate bar can contribute to daily iron intake, especially in vegetarian diets.

items.title: Mood improvement
items.content: Caffeine and theobromine in chocolate stimulate serotonin production, enhancing mood.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Excessive consumption may lead to weight gain and increase the risk of cavities.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The cookie typically contains wheat flour, making it unsuitable for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Chocolate often contains milk; those with lactose intolerance should choose a dairy‑free version.

items.title: Caffeine
items.content: Caffeine can cause insomnia or rapid heartbeat in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The bar is convenient to eat straight from the wrapper, can be added to yogurt, ice cream, or used as a flavorful filling in baked goods.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep in an airtight container to prevent moisture absorption.
